scope: Trace the deferred-apply consumers for opcodes 0x012E/0x016B/0x016F/0x0131. The receiver-apply-findings pass classified these as event-condition / deferred-apply receivers that construct queued event-condition objects (NoticeBlock/TalkBlock/PushBlock variants for the 3 event-condition opcodes; EndClientOrderEventReceiver for 0x0131) rather than mutating actor state directly. This follows those constructed objects through their vftables to identify which Lua callbacks fire when the queue is drained.
summary: Deferred Lua firers identified for 3 of 4 traced opcodes. NoticeBlock/NoticeNonBlock/TalkBlock/TalkNonBlock/PushBlock/PushNonBlock share a 12-slot vftable layout (offsets 0x00..0x2C, RTTI at 0x30). Base class slots 0x0C (FUN_00897660) and 0x10 (FUN_008977b0) fire _onPreEvent and _onPostEvent respectively via FUN_00447260 + FUN_00cc7a90 - shared across all 6 event-condition classes. Slot 0x28 is per-class and fires a family-specific Lua callback via the same FUN_00447260 pattern: TalkBlock -> _onTalkEvent, TalkNonBlock -> _onTalkRequest, PushBlock -> _onPushEvent, PushNonBlock -> _onPushRequest. NoticeBlock and NoticeNonBlock slot 0x28 are empty noops (FUN_008927e0, FUN_00892850 just `return`). EndClientOrderEventReceiver (0x0131) uses a different pattern: queues a new instance of itself, then drains via a switch dispatcher FUN_008a13a0 (slot 0x0C of its 5-slot vtable) that routes to FUN_006e1080..e0 thin wrappers and ultimately to FUN_008934a0/3520/35b0/3800 which mutate a target-object's state flags (target_object = *(receiver+8); writes to target+0x07/+0x1c/+0x1d/+0x22 byte fields, clears target+8). NO Lua fires in the EndClientOrderEvent dispatch chain. NO canonical CharaBase/PlayerBase/NpcBase actor-state writes from any of the 4 opcodes - the deferred patterns target either Lua callbacks (event-conditions) or sub-object state flags (client-order context).

structuralFindings: All 6 event-condition classes share an EventCondition base class with 5 virtual methods at slots 0x04..0x10 plus a per-class execute virtual at slot 0x28 dispatched indirectly from slot 0x04.

_onPreEvent and _onPostEvent fire from the base class on EVERY event-condition execution regardless of family (Notice/Talk/Push) or variant (Block/NonBlock). The 3 event-condition opcodes (0x012E + 0x016B + 0x016F) all funnel into these 2 shared callbacks.

Per-family slot 0x28 callbacks: TalkBlock fires _onTalkEvent, TalkNonBlock fires _onTalkRequest, PushBlock fires _onPushEvent, PushNonBlock fires _onPushRequest. NoticeBlock and NoticeNonBlock slot 0x28 are deliberate empty noops, suggesting the Notice variants only need the generic _onPreEvent/_onPostEvent hooks.

EndClientOrderEvent (0x0131) uses a structurally different queueing pattern: the receiver queues an instance of itself (not a separate Block/NonBlock class). The consumer dispatch in slot 0x0c (FUN_008a13a0) is a switch on a byte field that routes to 4 thin wrapper functions (FUN_006e1080..e0), which call deeper handlers (FUN_008934a0/3520/35b0/3800) that mutate state-flag bytes on a target object stored at *(receiver+8). No Lua fires in this chain.

The receiver-apply-findings pass's structural conclusion stands: the wire-confirmed deferred-apply receivers do NOT contribute new chain-key writes to data_dependency_catalog because they either fire Lua callbacks (event-conditions) or mutate sub-object state on classes that have no N-API readers (EndClientOrderEvent's target context).

inlineStorageFinding.description: Event-condition objects are stored INLINE in their receivers (not heap-allocated and queued). Receiver layout: receiver's own vftable at +0, secondary EventCondition vftable at +4 (SetTalk/SetNotice) or +0x58 (SetPush). Multi-inheritance: the receiver is BOTH a Receiver and an EventCondition; the secondary vftable lets external code dispatch on the receiver via its EventCondition identity.
inlineStorageFinding.implication: There is no separate queue holding event-condition pointers. The receiver instances live in the global dispatch table; the queue drainer iterates receivers and calls EventCondition virtual methods on their secondary-vftable sub-object.

addendum.actorStateWriteSearchResult: EXHAUSTIVELY NEGATIVE for the 3 event-condition opcodes (0x012E/0x016B/0x016F). No synchronous C++ writes to CharaBase / PlayerBase / NpcBase / DirectorBase / NpcBase fields occur in the Receive -> apply-helper -> ctor -> post-construct chain. The actor-state mutations the user goal expected ('the deferred patterns ultimately must touch state somewhere') happen via Lua scripts: the Lua handlers for _onPreEvent / _onPostEvent / _onTalkEvent / _onTalkRequest / _onPushEvent / _onPushRequest call N-API methods whose implementations write actor state. Those N-API implementations are scoped to WS-C (N-API implementation scaling beyond pilot), not to any specific event-condition opcode.
addendum.ws-fConclusion: WS-F (event-condition queue drainer trace) closed with structural finding: no synchronous C++ chain-key writes exist for opcodes 0x012E/0x016B/0x016F. The deferred pattern delegates actor-state mutation to Lua scripts that respond to the 6 documented apply-chain firers. The queue itself is a callback registry (FUN_0058B110 / FUN_00586810); identifying the drainer entry would only confirm the Lua-fire path which is already documented in lua_to_opcode.json via the bindingFlavor: deferred_via_event_condition entries.
